title: Fixed 4-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/SiO2/Ta2O5)
scientific_hypothesis: A fixed 4-layer MgF2/SiO2/Ta2O5 stack tests whether the proposed optical mechanism can balance the shared spectral targets, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness.
design_principle: Quarter-wave-like impedance matching using alternating high and low index materials. Starting with a low-index material (MgF2 or SiO2) on the substrate is hypothesized to be more robust for wide-angle performance than starting with high-index, based on standard AR design heuristics for glass substrates.
proposed_topology: exactly 4 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / MgF2
manufacturing_considerations: Independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm
Common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree
theory_basis: Standard quarter-wave AR theory suggests that n_layer = sqrt(n_air * n_substrate) minimizes reflection at a single wavelength. For broadband, multiple layers are needed. A 4-layer system offers 4 thickness variables to tune the spectral response.
expected_advantages: Lowest material cost and shortest deposition time among multi-layer options.
Simpler fabrication process reduces risk of interfacial defects.
known_risks: May not achieve <0.8% mean reflectance across the full 450-700 nm band at oblique angles.
High sensitivity to thickness errors due to fewer layers averaging out dispersion effects less effectively than thicker stacks.
execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness-optimization route for Fixed 4-layer analyze known stack route (MgF2/SiO2/Ta2O5). Use these declared media constraints: substrate: fused-silica; ambient: air; candidate_coating_materials: MgF2, SiO2, Al2O3, Ta2O5, TiO2. Use exactly 4 finite layers from the incident side: MgF2 / SiO2 / Ta2O5 / MgF2. Optimize every finite layer physical thickness with finite positive bounds. Evaluate the wavelength, incidence-angle, polarization, soft-objective, and uncertainty controls supplied below. Report verified optical metrics, total thickness, and manufacturing robustness; targets rank candidates and never gate physical validity. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees, 30 degrees, 45 degrees. polarization TE, TM. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: mean reflectance <= 0.8%; worst-case reflectance <= 3%; fewer layers; lower total physical thickness. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance. robustness conditions: independent one-sigma thickness error of 2 nm; common incidence-angle offset bounded by +/- 1 degree.
